text: A point f:A→R extends to K⊗ₖA by s⊗a↦s·f(a); restriction evaluates at 1⊗a. These inverse maps also preserve convolution, by the coproduct formula. The construction extends the module adjunction in [Stacks, tensor adjunction](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3) to bialgebra points over semirings. It is a monoid isomorphism; a Hopf structure additionally makes it a group isomorphism. Checks pass: [baseChangePointsMulEquiv_apply_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/BaseChange/Basic.lean#L108), [baseChangePointsMulEquiv_symm_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/BaseChange/Basic.lean#L115), [baseChangePointsMulEquiv_inv_apply_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/BaseChange/Basic.lean#L131).
Extension has the prescribed pure-tensor value.
Restriction has the inverse unit-tensor value.
With the additional Hopf hypothesis, inverse points have the antipode formula.

The extended point evaluates s⊗a as s·f(a), the usual formula behind [Stacks, tensor adjunction](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3). The dot is scalar multiplication through K→R, without division or rounding. The source verifies the algebra and convolution structures also over semirings; A need only be a bialgebra, while the value semiring R is commutative. Checks pass: [baseChangePointsMulEquiv_apply_ofConv](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/BaseChange/Basic.lean#L93), [baseChangePointsMulEquiv_mapDomain_apply_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/BaseChange/Naturality.lean#L113).
Forgetting convolution recovers the algebra tensor adjunction.
Precomposition gives the expected scalar times f(φ(a)).

Restriction takes a K-algebra point g of K⊗ₖA to a↦g(1⊗a), exactly the inverse formula of [Stacks, tensor adjunction](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3). The value algebra retains its elements and acquires the restricted k-action. This uses the specified compatible scalar actions, but neither flatness nor injectivity of A→K⊗ₖA is needed. Checks pass: [baseChangePointsMulEquiv_symm_ofConv](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/BaseChange/Basic.lean#L100), [pointToGeneralLinear_baseChangeMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/BaseChange.lean#L490).
The inverse is the algebra-adjunction restriction.
An actual GL consumer reads the same matrix on the restricted point.

Extending a point and then applying a K-algebra map φ:R→S equals extending φ∘f. On s⊗a both sides give s·φ(f(a)), since φ preserves the K-action. This is naturality of the tensor-adjunction formula in [Stacks, tensor adjunction](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3); the original point uses φ with scalars restricted to k. Checks pass: [baseChangePointsMulEquiv_apply_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/BaseChange/Basic.lean#L108), [baseChangePointsMulEquiv_symm_mapValue](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/BaseChange/Naturality.lean#L75).
Extension is computed on pure tensors.
The inverse restriction also commutes with the value-algebra map.

Restricting φ∘g along a↦1⊗a gives the same point as applying φ after restricting g. Both values are φ(g(1⊗a)). This is the inverse naturality square for [Stacks, tensor adjunction](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3), with φ a K-algebra map and compatible k-actions explicitly supplied. No inverse of φ or injectivity hypothesis is involved. Checks pass: [baseChangePointsMulEquiv_symm_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/BaseChange/Basic.lean#L115), [mapValue_baseChangePointsMulEquiv](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/BaseChange/Naturality.lean#L62).
Restriction is evaluation on unit tensors.
The forward extension satisfies the matching naturality square.

Precomposing a point by a bialgebra map φ:A→B commutes with scalar extension, provided φ becomes id_K⊗φ on the extended coordinates. Both constructions evaluate s⊗a as s·f(φ(a)). This combines the tensor formula of [Stacks, tensor adjunction](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3) with coproduct preservation; neither coordinate algebra must be commutative, and no flatness is required. Checks pass: [baseChangePointsMulEquiv_mapDomain_apply_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/BaseChange/Naturality.lean#L113), [baseChangePointsMulEquiv_symm_mapDomain](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/BaseChange/Naturality.lean#L121), [mapDomain_pointsBaseChange](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/BaseChange/Naturality.lean#L147).
The two operations have the expected pure-tensor value.
The inverse restriction commutes with the same coordinate map.
Base-valued points satisfy the actual scalar-extension specialization.

A commutative Hopf algebra H determines a group object by reversing its coordinate-algebra arrows: coproduct, counit and antipode become multiplication, identity and inverse, as in [Milne, §§3.1–3.5](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=75). The defined carrier is H in the opposite category of commutative algebras, with the existing group structure; it is not the set of elements of H. Checks pass: [grpObjPointsMulEquiv_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/Yoneda.lean#L338), [grpObjPointsMulEquiv_symm_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/Yoneda.lean#L373).
Its generalized points recover the underlying algebra-valued points.
Conversely, algebra-valued points recover categorical points.

A Hopf morphism f:H→K represents a group-object map from the object of K to that of H. It is the opposite of the underlying algebra map, matching the reversal in [Milne, §§3.1–3.5](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=75). Preservation of the coproduct and counit makes it preserve multiplication and identity; no finite-type or smoothness hypothesis is imposed. Checks pass: [grpObjMap_unop](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/Basic.lean#L79), [grpObjPointsMulEquiv_comp_grpObjMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/Yoneda.lean#L386).
Reversing back recovers the given coordinate morphism.
On generalized points this map becomes precomposition by f.

Reversing the represented group-object arrow back to coordinates recovers exactly f’s algebra morphism. This is the coordinate reversal of [Stacks, affine morphisms](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01I1), implemented here directly in the opposite algebra category. The equality identifies the chosen map itself, rather than merely asserting existence of some map with isomorphic source and target. Checks pass: [grpObjMap_unop_hom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/Basic.lean#L84), [quotientGrpObjInclusion_unop](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Categorical.lean#L58).
The underlying algebra homomorphism is unchanged.
The quotient inclusion has the prescribed coordinate quotient map.

After reversing the group-object arrow and forgetting categorical packaging, its algebra homomorphism is precisely the one underlying f. Thus each coordinate has its original image, consistent with [Stacks, affine morphisms](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01I1). The Hopf compatibility remains a property of this same function; the equality introduces no new coordinate transformation or assumption that f is injective. Checks pass: [grpObjMap_unop](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/Basic.lean#L79), [grpObjPointsMulEquiv_comp_grpObjMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/Yoneda.lean#L386).
The bundled coordinate morphism is already identical.
Evaluation on generalized points uses this same coordinate map.

Taking the product with the identity group-object map corresponds on coordinates to id_H⊗f. This is the tensor-product description of products in [Milne, §§3.1–3.5](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=75): the first coordinate factor stays fixed and f acts on the second. The statement identifies a tensor map, and does not assert that either factor embeds in the tensor product. Checks pass: [grpObjMap_unop_hom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/Basic.lean#L84), [grpObjPointsMulEquiv_comp_grpObjMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/Yoneda.lean#L386).
The second-factor map is the original algebra homomorphism.
The represented map acts by the matching coordinate precomposition.

Two coordinate Hopf morphisms are equal if their represented group-object maps agree: reversing the arrows recovers the underlying algebra maps, and Hopf morphisms are determined by those maps. This matches the uniqueness in [Stacks, affine morphisms](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01I1). Injectivity here concerns the assignment between morphism sets; it does not say that each individual morphism is injective. Checks pass: [grpObjMap_unop_hom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/Basic.lean#L84), [grpObjMap_id](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/Basic.lean#L109).
Equality of represented maps recovers equality of algebra maps.
The identity coordinate map has the expected represented map.

Composing coordinate maps H→K→L gives the reverse composite of represented group-object maps, from the object of L through K to H. This is precisely the opposite-category convention behind [Stacks, affine morphisms](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01I1). The symbol ≫ means perform its left map first; the reversal is categorical, not a reversal of multiplication inside H. Checks pass: [grpObjMap_id](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/Basic.lean#L109), [grpObjPointsMulEquiv_comp_grpObjMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/Yoneda.lean#L386).
The corresponding identity law holds.
Composition with a represented map agrees with point precomposition.

The represented map preserves both group-object identity and multiplication, because the coordinate morphism preserves counit and coproduct. These are the reversed diagrams in [Milne, §§3.1–3.5](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=75). Although the name says monoid morphism, its source and target are group objects, so inverse preservation follows automatically; this is a proof of compatibility, not additional map data. Checks pass: [quotientGrpObjInclusion_isMonHom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Categorical.lean#L66), [grpObjPointsMulEquiv_comp_grpObjMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/Yoneda.lean#L386).
The actual Hopf-ideal quotient inclusion inherits both monoid laws.
The represented map agrees with the convolution-group point map.

A coordinate Hopf morphism φ:H→K sends every A-valued point f of K to f∘φ. Coproduct and counit preservation make this a group homomorphism for convolution, and associativity of composition gives naturality in A, as in [Milne, §§3.1–3.5](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=75). Points range over commutative algebras, not merely fields or base-ring-valued points. Checks pass: [mapPointsFunctor_app_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/Basic.lean#L153), [mapPointsFunctor_naturality_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/Basic.lean#L168), [quotientPointsHom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Basic.lean#L74).
Each component is the specified precomposition.
Postcomposition in the value algebra commutes with that operation.
The native Hopf-ideal quotient consumer uses this point map.

The component at A sends the algebra map f:K→A to f∘φ:H→A, as expected from [Milne, §§3.1–3.5](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=75). The WithConv wrapper keeps that same function while giving points their convolution group law. It does not make point multiplication ordinary function composition; precomposition here is only the action of the coordinate morphism. Checks pass: [mapPointsFunctor_app_apply_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/Basic.lean#L161), [quotientPointsHom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Basic.lean#L74).
Evaluation gives f(φ(h)) on each coordinate.
Quotient points specialize this same precomposition formula.

At a coordinate h, the transported point has value f(φ(h)). Thus the formal component really is pullback of an algebra-valued point along the coordinate morphism, as in [Milne, §§3.1–3.5](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=75). Removing the convolution wrapper exposes ordinary evaluation; it does not change the point’s function or introduce any transpose, inverse or scalar extension. Checks pass: [mapPointsFunctor_app_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/Basic.lean#L153), [quotientPointsHom_apply_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Basic.lean#L82).
The complete point is the composite algebra map.
For quotient points the coordinate is mapped to its quotient class.

Changing the value algebra by χ:A→B and pulling back along φ:H→K commute: both give h↦χ(f(φ(h))). This is the naturality required for group-valued points in [Milne, §§3.1–3.5](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=75). The value-algebra arrow acts forward, whereas the coordinate arrow acts backward; commutative rings and algebra morphisms are the stated setting. Checks pass: [mapPointsFunctor_app_apply_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/Basic.lean#L161), [mapPoints_quotientPointsHom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Naturality.lean#L41).
The coordinate pullback has the claimed evaluation.
The native quotient-point inclusion satisfies this naturality equation.

If φ:H→K is surjective, two A-valued points of K agreeing after precomposition agree on every element of K, by choosing a preimage. Hence the induced point map is injective, consistent with coordinate reversal in [Stacks, affine morphisms](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01I1). This concerns all commutative value algebras A; no field or reducedness hypothesis is needed. Checks pass: [quotientPointsHom_injective](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Basic.lean#L104), [mapPointsFunctor_app_apply_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/Basic.lean#L161).
The surjective Hopf-ideal quotient yields an injective point map.
Agreement after precomposition is exactly agreement on φ(h).

Precomposing with the identity coordinate morphism fixes every algebra-valued point. Consequently the entire natural transformation is the identity, including its group-homomorphism components. This is the identity law for the functor-of-points construction in [Milne, §§3.1–3.5](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=75); the convolution wrapper and categorical packaging leave the underlying function unchanged. Checks pass: [mapPointsFunctor_app_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/Basic.lean#L153), [mapPointsFunctor_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/Basic.lean#L199).
The component reduces to precomposition with the identity.
The matching reverse-composition law also holds.

For H→K→L, pulling an L-point back along the composite equals first pulling it to K and then to H. Associativity of algebra-map composition proves equality of natural transformations, as in [Milne, §§3.1–3.5](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=75). The order reverses because coordinate arrows reverse on points; the convolution group itself need not be commutative. Checks pass: [mapPointsFunctor_comp_app_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/Basic.lean#L213), [mapPointsFunctor_eq_quotientPointsHom_of_mkQuotient_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Basic.lean#L92).
The identity is verified on individual algebra-valued points.
A morphism factoring through a Hopf quotient satisfies the corresponding two-step point formula.

The composite coordinate map acts on a point by two successive precompositions, first with the second coordinate map and then with the first. This explicit component equation checks the arrow convention of [Milne, §§3.1–3.5](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=75). All points have the same value algebra A, and the formula uses neither multiplication of points nor an inverse map. Checks pass: [mapPointsFunctor_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/Basic.lean#L199), [mapPointsFunctor_eq_quotientPointsHom_of_mkQuotient_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Basic.lean#L92).
The equation holds for the full natural transformations.
The native quotient-factorization consumer uses this exact composition order.

This assigns to H the group-valued functor A↦Hom_R-alg(H,A), with convolution multiplication, and sends coordinate maps to precomposition. Using the opposite Hopf category records the reversed arrows of [Milne, §§3.1–3.5](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=75); maps between value algebras still act forward. It packages these operations and their laws without imposing finite type or asserting the full scheme equivalence. Checks pass: [pointsFunctor_obj](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/Basic.lean#L235), [pointsFunctor_map_app_apply_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/Basic.lean#L249), [mapPointsFunctor_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/Basic.lean#L199).
The object assignment is exactly the existing algebra-valued points functor.
The morphism assignment evaluates by coordinate precomposition.
The defining reverse-composition law holds.

The arrow assigned to a morphism in the opposite Hopf category is precisely precomposition by its underlying coordinate map. This identifies the actual natural transformation used in the functor, matching the arrow reversal of [Milne, §§3.1–3.5](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=75). Reversing the categorical wrapper changes direction, not the algebra homomorphism’s values or the points’ convolution law. Checks pass: [pointsFunctor_map_app_apply_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/Basic.lean#L249), [mapPointsFunctor_naturality_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/Basic.lean#L168).
Individual coordinate evaluations expose the assigned map.
Its components commute with maps of value algebras.

A point f transported by an opposite-coordinate arrow evaluates h as f(φ(h)), where φ is the underlying coordinate homomorphism in the reverse direction. This is the concrete functor-of-points rule of [Milne, §§3.1–3.5](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=75). The source spells out both reversals explicitly; unwrapping the convolution point simply reveals its original algebra-map function. Checks pass: [mapPointsFunctor_app_apply_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/Basic.lean#L161), [pointsFunctor_map](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/CommHopfAlgCat/Basic.lean#L242).
The underlying natural transformation has exactly this evaluation rule.
The outer functor chooses that natural transformation.

Multiplicativity means that the norm of a product equals the product of the norms, strengthening the usual submultiplicative inequality. This declaration isolates that equation: its assumptions supply only multiplication and a real-valued function. Nonnegativity, separation, a triangle inequality, and normalization at one must come from additional structure. Compared with [Klazar, Lecture1 p11](https://kam.mff.cuni.cz/~klazar/MAIII_lec1_26.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Ring/Basic.lean#L722).

Here a ring homomorphism is called isometric when it preserves the supplied norm functions. The declaration itself assumes no metric, and does not assert injectivity. For compatible seminormed rings, preservation of differences gives distance preservation; separation of the source norm then gives injectivity. Surjectivity is not required. Compared with [Erdman §1.2.12](https://web.pdx.edu/~erdman/OpAlg/operator_algebras_pdf.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Ring/Basic.lean#L694).

A bounded ring homomorphism satisfies ‖f(x)‖≤C‖x‖ for every x, using one positive real constant C. This is a uniform growth bound, not a bounded image: the identity on the real numbers qualifies with C=1. The source permits seminorms and requires neither completeness nor a scalar-linear structure. Compared with [Erdman §§2.2.2,3.1.1](https://web.pdx.edu/~erdman/OpAlg/operator_algebras_pdf.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Ring/Basic.lean#L491).

A multiplicative seminorm normalized by ‖1‖=1 becomes a map to the real numbers preserving zero, one, and multiplication. It is not asserted to preserve addition: ordinary absolute value already fails that condition. The domain may be noncommutative, and the seminorm may vanish on nonzero elements. Compared with [Klazar, Lecture1 p11](https://kam.mff.cuni.cz/~klazar/MAIII_lec1_26.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Ring/Basic.lean#L746).

The same normalized multiplicative seminorm can be recorded as a map into the nonnegative real numbers. It preserves zero, one, and multiplication, with the same numerical values as the real norm. This codomain contains only finite values; it is distinct from the nonnegative extended reals, which also contain infinity. Compared with [Klazar, Lecture1 p11](https://kam.mff.cuni.cz/~klazar/MAIII_lec1_26.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Ring/Basic.lean#L754).

The formula ‖ab‖=‖a‖‖b‖ is available whenever multiplicativity of the chosen norm function is assumed. This theorem exposes that equation without adding ring or metric hypotheses. In particular, the name alone does not imply that the function is nonnegative or separates zero; those properties need their own assumptions. Compared with [Klazar, Lecture1 p11](https://kam.mff.cuni.cz/~klazar/MAIII_lec1_26.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Ring/Basic.lean#L726).

For a multiplicative seminorm with ‖1‖=1, the norm of a natural power is the corresponding power of the norm. The exponent includes zero: both sides then equal one, even when the base is zero. No inverse, negative exponent, commutativity, or separation assumption is needed. Compared with [Klazar, Lecture1 p11](https://kam.mff.cuni.cz/~klazar/MAIII_lec1_26.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Ring/Basic.lean#L761).

The norm of a finite product equals the product of the norms when the seminorm is multiplicative and normalized at one. Commutativity makes the unordered product well-defined. An empty product equals one on both sides; equal values at different indices remain separate factors, and no convergence assumption is involved. Compared with [Klazar, Lecture1 p11](https://kam.mff.cuni.cz/~klazar/MAIII_lec1_26.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Ring/Basic.lean#L793).

In a seminormed ring, the norm of a product is bounded by the product of the norms. This requires neither a multiplicative identity nor commutative multiplication, and the seminorm may vanish on nonzero elements. Equality is a stronger property and is not asserted by this general ring inequality. Compared with [Erdman §3.1.1](https://web.pdx.edu/~erdman/OpAlg/operator_algebras_pdf.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Ring/Basic.lean#L218).

Submultiplicativity bounds ‖aⁿ‖ by ‖a‖ⁿ for every natural exponent when ‖1‖=1. The normalization handles n=0, including a=0, since zero powers equal one. For positive exponents the corresponding bound needs no normalization at one. Multiplication may be noncommutative, and equality is not claimed. Compared with [Erdman §3.1.1](https://web.pdx.edu/~erdman/OpAlg/operator_algebras_pdf.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Ring/Basic.lean#L417).

A finite product in a normed commutative ring has norm at most the product of its factors’ norms, provided ‖1‖=1. That extra condition covers the empty product. Repeated values at different indices contribute repeatedly; the statement concerns finite multiplication, with no convergence or completeness assumption. Compared with [Erdman §3.1.1](https://web.pdx.edu/~erdman/OpAlg/operator_algebras_pdf.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Ring/Basic.lean#L370).

The norm of the natural number n interpreted inside a seminormed ring is at most n‖1‖. Inside the ring, n means adding one n times; on the right, n is an ordinary real number. No characteristic-zero hypothesis is needed: the ring element may even be zero for positive n. Compared with [Faris §§16.2,23.3](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Ring/Basic.lean#L336).

For a nonzero element of a normed division ring, the extended norm of its inverse is the reciprocal of its extended norm. The nonzero condition matters: Lean defines the ring inverse of zero as zero, but the reciprocal of zero in the nonnegative extended reals is infinity. Compared with [Klazar, Lecture1 Ex.23](https://kam.mff.cuni.cz/~klazar/MAIII_lec1_26.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Field/Basic.lean#L86).

The real numbers carry their usual field operations and absolute-value norm. Multiplicativity is the familiar identity |xy|=|x||y|, and the inherited distance is |x−y|. This declaration packages that standard normed-field structure; it does not choose a new topology or assert completeness as part of the definition. Compared with [Klazar, Lecture1 p11](https://kam.mff.cuni.cz/~klazar/MAIII_lec1_26.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Field/Basic.lean#L302).

The ordinary absolute-value norm on the real numbers has dense range among nonnegative reals; indeed, every nonnegative real is its own absolute value. Thus every interval with 0≤x<y contains a norm strictly between x and y. Negative intervals and intervals with equal endpoints are outside the assertion. Compared with [Faris §16.2](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Field/Basic.lean#L306).

A densely normed field is nontrivially normed because some norm lies strictly between one and two. This gives the required element with norm greater than one while retaining the original field and norm. The converse is not asserted: a nontrivial norm may have a discrete set of positive values. Compared with [Klazar, Lecture1 pp10–11](https://kam.mff.cuni.cz/~klazar/MAIII_lec1_26.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Field/Basic.lean#L182).

A normed field supplies a normed commutative ring with exactly the same operations, norm, and metric. Multiplicativity implies the ring’s required submultiplicative inequality. This conversion does not change distances or forget separation; it simply makes results requiring only a normed ring available without requiring them to mention division. Compared with [Klazar, Lecture1 p11](https://kam.mff.cuni.cz/~klazar/MAIII_lec1_26.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Field/Basic.lean#L195).

The multiplicative identity in a normed division ring has norm one. Multiplicativity makes its norm an idempotent real number, and separation excludes zero because the identity is nonzero. The proof works without commutative multiplication; this normalization follows from the division-ring structure rather than being an extra choice. Compared with [Klazar, Lecture1 Ex.23](https://kam.mff.cuni.cz/~klazar/MAIII_lec1_26.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Field/Basic.lean#L66).

A normed ring with a multiplicative norm has no zero divisors: if ab=0, then ‖a‖‖b‖=0, so one factor has zero norm and therefore is zero. Separation is essential; a zero seminorm would not justify this conclusion. Neither commutative multiplication nor existence of inverses is required. Compared with [Klazar, Lecture1 p11](https://kam.mff.cuni.cz/~klazar/MAIII_lec1_26.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Ring/Basic.lean#L839).

A normed commutative ring also satisfies the requirements of a seminormed commutative ring using its existing operations, norm, and distance. The weaker structure does not demand separation, but the conversion makes no quotient and changes no values. In particular, it does not impose the additional normalization ‖1‖=1. Compared with [Erdman §§1.2,3.1.1](https://web.pdx.edu/~erdman/OpAlg/operator_algebras_pdf.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Ring/Basic.lean#L153).

For a smooth homomorphism of finite-dimensional real Lie groups, this is its differential at the identity, expressed using left-invariant derivations. It is linear and preserves brackets; connectedness is unnecessary. Smoothness ensures the derivative is genuine, despite Lean’s zero default for nondifferentiable maps. Identity, composition and compatibility with exponentials are proved alongside it. See [Lee, Theorem 8.44, Propositions 8.45 and 20.8(g)](https://julianchaidez.net/materials/reu/lee_smooth_manifolds.pdf) and [the defining differential comparison](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Geometry/Lie/Functor.lean#L198). Native Checks pass: [functor laws](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Geometry/Lie/Functor.lean#L220), [algebra maps on units](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Geometry/Lie/AlgebraHom.lean#L58), and [the Spin projection differential](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Geometry/Lie/CliffordAlgebra/Spin/Differential.lean#L242), with [Spin(3) identified with SU(2) and its conjugation action](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/CliffordAlgebra/Spin/Real/Three.lean#L351).
Evaluation at identity gives the genuine differential.
Differentiating the identity gives the identity.
Differentiation respects composition in the stated order.
The smooth homomorphism intertwines exponential maps.
For an algebra map on units, its differential is that algebra map.
The actual Spin projection differential is the normalized bivector/skew-matrix equivalence.
